nodes.title: D5 empty turns read as SILENCE (main 2026-10-21, the owner's census F5 + 14.4's safeguard check-in tier; evals/duplex-2026-10/phantom-empty.mjs, results/phantom-empty-{owner,phone}.json). Method: a fresh live Voice Live D5 pass over all 66 bake scenarios, owner and phone-echo variants (today's ear, audio times recorded), then the SAME recorded ear events replayed through the base engine (int/r5-rel144 @ b8285b2b) and the fixed one; every empty commit classified against the gold (child speech under the ear item ≥ 150 ms = unheard; her playback only = echo; neither = noise; no item = no_item; the floor's hold offer). BEFORE: owner 7 empty of 46 commits (4 unheard, 3 hold offer), phone 6 of 44 (5 unheard, 1 hold offer); true phantoms (echo / noise / no item) 0 of 90 commits; every unheard turn reached the server as "" + asrConfidence 0 → cls source empty → isSilentTurn: a child who SPOKE read as silent in 9 of 90 commits (10%). AFTER: false silences 0 of 9 (each marked duplex.unheard → source asr); commit streams identical in all 132 runs (time and text); the new no-item drop fired 9 times, each on an empty SPEAK the base engine also never posted (held: one turn at a time). Earlier recorded arms agree (d5v200.owner 4 unheard + 3 hold offer; d5r11.owner 5 + 2). The harness's stereo AEC produced no echo-opened empty items; a real phone's may (production census F5) — only the item-less case is guarded at the client.

D5: an empty turn over speech the ear could not read is UNHEARD, never silence. The client marks it (duplex.unheard, set only when Voice Live's own item ended with no words since the last commit) and never posts an empty SPEAK with no ear item behind it (the safety floor and the hold offer untouched); the server classifies an unheard turn as source asr; the Director asks again with its own shape (unheardAgain: her ear, not their fault) and never counts it toward the are-you-there break; in an open safeguard CHECK-IN an unheard turn re-asks the check-in and does not use up its one silence, failing closed on the THIRD unheard turn in a row (UNHEARD_CHECKS = 2). Reversal: production traces showing unheard turns that were really silence (the ear opening an item on room noise), or a child whose distress went unescalated behind repeated unheard turns.

D5 drops the child's words said OVER her line (census F5 #1, main's priority: the topic request lost in a barge-in merge; evals/duplex-2026-10/results/lost-words.json). Method: the live Voice Live D5 events of all 66 scenarios, owner + phone variants, replayed through the engine before / after; an ear final with content words (not a continuer / stop / hold phrase) that no commit carried is LOST. BEFORE: 12 content finals lost (owner 7, phone 5): every barge_fold_in (0/5 committed in EVERY D5 arm ever recorded, d5r5…d5v200, while D4-full committed 4/5) and the content barge_stops ("8 minutes duty"). Cause: over her playback the device detects the child's onset late (her echo masks it; 2,620 ms vs the ear's 1,996 in fold_in-0389), the fold-in carries the turn from that late onset, and the fan-in (server/duplex/fanin.js belongs) admitted only items that started after it — the burst's own item, with the words, was dropped as the old turn's; with no partials on D5 the words always land after her line, so the her-floor lexical yield never saw them either. AFTER (an item still open at the carried onset, opened ≤ 1.2 s before it, with a known audio end past it, joins): content lost 12 → 1 (phone barge_stop 0386 left); fold-ins committed owner 0/5 → 5/5, phone 0/5 → 3/5 (the other two heard "Yes." / nothing); control phrases unchanged (11 / 11, never turns); the duplex scorer's floor metrics unchanged on both variants (cut-offs, continuers, phantom, EOT p50/p90, skeleton CER) except lone words noticed 5/8 → 6/8. The carried request words also leaked into the HOLD OFFER (base already did on hold_long: "रुको, रुको।" sent as the offer's words, which the server reads as words, not a hold check-in): the hold offer is now always wordless (2 → 0 per variant).

The fold-in's carried turn keeps the burst's OWN ear item: an item still open at the carried onset (opened at most CARRY_PRE_MS = 1,200 ms before it, with a KNOWN audio end past it) belongs to the turn; the hold offer after "wait" is always wordless. Not changed (tried, no effect on the 132 recorded runs): carrying a hushed burst at her_end when her line did not hand over (governor carryCheck) — kept as a candidate if production shows a request said over an explanation, read as a short burst, lost. Reversal: production traces showing the previous turn's words (an echo item, the last answer) folded into the next turn.

The echo filters ate the child's words with ONE-letter skeletons, the negation first (census F5 #2; the owner's e6392332 t14-15: नहीं→n, रहा→r, आप→p, क्या→k, है/हो/आ→empty stripped, "I don't understand" became "I understand something"; evals/duplex-2026-10/negation-echo.mjs, results/negation-echo.json). Cause: "नहीं" = "n" = her "हैं" / tag "ना" / "हाँ", and short runs of one-letter skeletons match her Roman Hinglish ("aap kya" → p k took the child's own "आप क्या"). Method: 41,259 distinct (her line → the child's heard reply) pairs of the cached sim lab voice records (20,109 with a negation), text level, base filters (int @ b8285b2b) vs fixed; floors: her own line fed back as echo in the same script, and CROSS-SCRIPT (her Roman line through the rules transliterator, as the ear writes her echo: 35,962 lines). Fixed (a negation keys on one class across scripts, नहीं/nahi → ¬nahi; a run of her words counts only with a match of 2+ letters; the whole-text echo share needs one too): replies losing a negation 510 → 169 (the rest: the child repeating her phrase, negation and all, in a long-anchored run); negated replies read whole as echo by the cascade lane's isEcho 1,823 → 937; child words removed in all 36,556 → 32,864; floors: same script 2,029 → 2,053 tokens left, cross-script 15,521 → 15,689 (+1%). The first cut pushed at d5788971 (negation keyed on its SURFACE) broke her cross-script echo runs at every negation: cross-script floor 15,521 → 22,761 (superseded here). Main's literal bar (a negation NEVER subtracted) measured: negation loss 0, but floors 2,029 → 10,917 and 15,521 → 23,824 (her own echoed negations leak into the child's turn, a stray "nahi" beside the child's "haan"). D5 bake replay (132 runs): 0 commits changed.

Echo matching (src/lesson/cascadeLink.ts echoKey, shared by the duplex EchoSubtractor and isEcho): a negation keys on ONE class across scripts (नहीं / नही / nahi / nahin → ¬nahi; ना / na; मत / mat; no; not …), never its consonant skeleton; a run of her words is echo only with at least one match of two letters or more, and the whole-text echo share needs one too — so a one-letter skeleton (नहीं, रहा, आप, क्या) never anchors a removal, while her Roman line echoed back in Devanagari still goes. Main's literal "never subtracted" bar was measured and is left to main (see ms-r144-negation-echo). Reversal: device traces with her echo leaking short words into the child's turn, or a child's negation still removed inside a long run.

Not shipped: carrying a hushed burst over her line into the next turn at her_end when her line did NOT hand over (governor carryCheck: its words decide, a lone continuer or no words drop back to idle). Measured on the 132 recorded D5 runs (66 scenarios × owner + phone): 0 commits changed with it on or off, before and after the fan-in fix (the fold-in path, phase overlap at her_end, already carries; the loss was the fan-in's). Revisit only if production shows a request said over an explanation, read as a short burst, lost.

How often three UNHEARD turns come in a row (main's check before relying on the check-in's fail-closed). The 132 recorded D5 runs are single exchanges: no run holds two unheard turns (max 1). Per committed turn, unheard is 4/53 = 7.5 % (owner) and 5/48 = 10.4 % (phone echo) after the fixes; the bake over-represents hard tails. If turns were independent, P(≥ 3 in a row in a lesson) = 0.7 % / 1.1 % / 1.9 % (owner, 20 / 30 / 50 turns) and 1.8 % / 2.8 % / 4.8 % (phone) — above main's ~1 in 100 bar on the phone variant; a bad microphone makes turns correlated (worse). No D5 production codes visible to this stream. Hence the tap path (safe:continue / safe:stop on every unheard wait) ships with it.
